amendments.because: Simplify a repeatedly reviewed area: ownership locks raced, so the owner's simple-rule preference wins; a killed review's folder waits a day for the sweep
amendments.done_when: Every review removes its forge-review-* folder and the git worktree registration it created, including when the review fails, is interrupted (Ctrl-C or the process killed and run again) or the worktree removal fails; and each review first deletes forge-review-* folders older than a day that no running review owns. A command-level test interrupts a review and shows its folder is gone afterwards, and another shows an old leftover folder is removed by the next review.

done_when: Every review removes its own forge-review-* folder when it finishes, fails or is interrupted with Ctrl-C; and each review first deletes forge-review-* folders whose last change is more than a day old, since no review runs that long, with no lock or ownership record. A folder left by a review that was killed outright is removed by the first review that runs a day later. Command-level tests: a failing and an interrupted review leave no folder, an old leftover folder is removed by the next review, and a fresh folder of another review is left alone.

findings.body: The previously reported gap remains: an aged leftover containing the mode-0500 `locked/inner` directories modeled in tests/test_reviews_remove_their_temp_folders.py:28–31 cannot be deleted by an ordinary user. `ignore_errors=True` suppresses the permission failures without repairing them, leaving the folder behind indefinitely. The current review's cleanup uses TemporaryDirectory at src/forge/review.py:396, which retries recoverable permission errors, but the sweep does not. Apply permission recovery during the sweep and verify it with an aged, read-only leftover. See the [Python rmtree contract](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/shutil.html#shutil.rmtree).
findings.title: Retry recoverable permission errors when sweeping stale folders

why: Reviews leave their forge-review-* temporary checkouts behind in the system temp folder (304 found on 2026-10-02, part of what filled the disk), because a review that is interrupted or whose worktree removal fails never deletes its folder
